issues.legal_issue: An appeal by one of several persons jointly affected by an order on a ground common to them does not abate in its entirety merely because another person joined as a respondent dies and that person’s heirs are not brought on the record.
material_facts: Several decree-holders jointly sought execution of their decree, but the executing court dismissed the application on a ground common to them.
Only one decree-holder appealed, joining the other decree-holders as respondents.
One respondent died during the appeal, and that respondent’s heirs were not brought on the record within the prescribed period.
The High Court held that the appeal had abated in its entirety because the order could not be varied for the surviving decree-holders without potentially inconsistent results.
issues.conclusion: The appeal did not abate in its entirety. The appellate court’s power to vary or modify the order under Order 41, Rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure was not lost because a jointly interested respondent died and that respondent’s heirs were not brought on the record.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 41, Rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure, where an order or decree proceeds on a ground common to several persons, an appeal by one of them may permit the appellate court to reverse or vary it in favour of all, whether the others are not parties to the appeal or are respondents. The power is not lost merely because a respondent who was jointly interested dies and that respondent’s heirs are not added. Ratan Lal Shah v. Firm Lalmandas Chhadammalal & Anr. was relied on; Rameshwar Prasad & Ors. v. M/s. Shyam Beharilal Jagannath & Ors. was distinguished because all the plaintiffs had appealed jointly in that case, whereas only one of the joint decree-holders appealed here.

rule.if: appeal_from_common_ground_order and joint_interest_in_order and one_interested_person_appeals and other_interested_persons_joined_as_respondents and respondent_dies_during_appeal and deceased_respondent_heirs_not_added_in_time

predicates.appeal_from_common_ground_order: The proceeding is an appeal from an order that rests on a ground common to several interested persons.
predicates.joint_interest_in_order: Several persons are jointly interested in the order or decree under appeal.
predicates.one_interested_person_appeals: One of the persons jointly affected by the order files the appeal without the others joining as appellants.
predicates.other_interested_persons_joined_as_respo: Other persons jointly affected by the order are joined as respondents in the appeal.
predicates.respondent_dies_during_appeal: A respondent jointly interested in the matter dies while the appeal is pending.
predicates.deceased_respondent_heirs_not_added_in_t: The deceased respondent’s heirs are not brought on the record within the applicable period.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns an order on a ground common to jointly interested persons, one of them appeals, the others are respondents, and a respondent dies without heirs being added in time, the appeal does not abate in its entirety.

issues.legal_issue: A pending proceeding does not abate merely because a party’s legal representative, who is already on the record in another capacity, has not been formally identified as a legal representative or other heirs have not been added within the prescribed period.
material_facts: The deceased respondent’s legal representative was already on the record as an appellant and was one of the heirs.
No formal application was made to identify that appellant on the record as the deceased respondent’s legal representative.
Other heirs were not brought on the record within the prescribed period.
issues.conclusion: The proceeding did not abate on this ground because a legal representative was already on the record in another capacity; failure to bring the other heirs on the record within the prescribed period did not cause abatement.
issues.legal_principle: Where a party dies and one legal representative is already on the record in another capacity, the representative may be identified as such by an appropriate application. The proceeding does not abate merely because other legal representatives were not brought on the record within the period prescribed by the Limitation Act. The Court stated this as an additional ground for rejecting abatement.

rule.if: pending_proceeding_after_party_death and legal_representative_already_on_record_in_another_capacity and legal_representative_is_an_heir and other_heirs_not_added_in_time

predicates.pending_proceeding_after_party_death: A proceeding remains pending after a party to it dies.
predicates.legal_representative_already_on_record_i: A person who represents the deceased party is already on the record in a capacity other than as that party’s legal representative.
predicates.legal_representative_is_an_heir: The person already on the record is an heir of the deceased party.
predicates.other_heirs_not_added_in_time: Other heirs of the deceased party are not brought on the record within the applicable period.

issues.definition: When a party dies during a pending proceeding and an heir who is a legal representative is already on the record in another capacity, the proceeding does not abate merely because other heirs are not added in time.
